contents.text: يا سيدنا حاز احسانا ومكرمة وفضله شاع في السبع الاقاليم / انعم بوعدك يا قمر البلاغة يا نسل الكرام ويا صدر المخادم
contents.note: 'al-aqalim' is written small and slanting above the start of line 2 as the overflow of line 1 (in the same black ink, not a red gloss); looks like a praise address (to the recipient, or a verse opening); 'ya sayyidana haza ihsanan wa-makrumatan wa-fadluhu sha'a fi l-sab' al-aqalim' = O our lord, who has won beneficence and nobility, whose merit is spread over the seven climes; 'an'im bi-wa'dika ya qamar al-balagha ya nasl al-kiram wa-ya sadr al-makhadim' = grant (us) by your promise, O moon of eloquence, O offspring of the generous, O chief of the (lords?) - last word makhadim uncertain

contents.text: وكتب انسان من اهل الرحبة يسمى [?] مرجان منها
contents.note: 'wa-kataba insan min ahl al-Rahba yusamma ...' = and a man from the people of al-Rahba (Rahba, the Euphrates town) wrote, called ... ; the name at the left end of the line is small and cramped, read as 'Marjan' only tentatively, 'minha' = from it/there

contents.word_groups: about 3-4 per line, roughly 28 (dividers not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; each line begins (at right) with a small double slash mark or a bare sign and ends at left with a dotted divider; the line-end divider carries on into the next line; signs: bracket/arch shapes, a ring-and-hook glyph (very frequent, c. 2 per line), V and W shapes, small circle, closed box

contents.text: فحللتها سريعا لسهولتها وهي [continues overleaf]
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuha sari'an li-suhulatiha wa-hiya' = I solved it quickly because of its ease, and it is (verse follows on next page, 25v)

correspondents.arabic: انسان من اهل الرحبة يسمى [?] مرجان
correspondents.translit: an unnamed man of al-Rahba, called (?) Marjan - reading of the name tentative

technique_remarks: only 'solved quickly because of its easiness' (feminine -ha: the cipher is referred to as a feminine noun, probably a qasida/risala); no trick described
plaintext_for: block on this page (lines 4-11); the plaintext itself starts on the next page (f. 25v) after the formula on line 12
certainty: medium: layout high, Arabic of lines 1-3 medium, name low; sign counts approximate; page has 12 lines not 13

contents.text: والله ما ندري اذا ما فاتنا طلب لك من الذي تطلب [?] / ولقد ضربنا في البلاد فلم نجد احدا سواك الى المكارم / ينسب
contents.note: a verse (rhymes in -b: 'tatlub' / 'yunsab', last word 'yunsab' alone at line start of line 3 as overflow); 'wa-llahi ma nadri idha ma fatana talabun laka mina lladhi tatlub / wa-la-qad darabna fi l-bilad fa-lam najid ahadan siwaka ila l-makarim yunsab' = by God we do not know (what to do) if your request escapes us from the one you seek; we have travelled the lands and found none but you attributed to noble deeds. Translation approximate; first hemistich words 'talab laka' and 'tatlub' not fully certain. It follows directly on the formula 'fa-halaltuha ... wa-hiya' at the foot of f. 25r

contents.word_groups: about 3 per line, roughly 22 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: introduced by 'wa-min dhalika' (and of that sort) written in Arabic at the right of line 4, with the first signs on the same line; new alphabet compared with 25r: X, K, triangle, I-bar, ring-with-bar shapes, plus a few hook glyphs from the previous block; lines end at left with a dotted divider

contents.text: فحللت ذلك لسهولته وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltu dhalika li-suhulatihi wa-huwa' = I solved that because of its ease, and it is

contents.text: قصدتك حين ضاق الامر لما رايت الدهر انشب مخلبيه / علمت ان غيرك ليس يرجى وانك كهف من ياوي اليه
contents.note: verse: 'qasadtuka hina daqa l-amr lamma ra'aytu l-dahr anshaba makhlabayhi / 'alimtu anna ghayraka laysa yurja wa-annaka kahfu man ya'wi ilayhi' = I came to you when things grew narrow, when I saw Time sink in its claws; I knew that none but you is to be hoped for and that you are the refuge of whoever seeks shelter; rhyme -ihi; 'rayta' vs 'ra'aytu' spelling: written without hamza

contents.text: ومن
contents.note: catchword at the lower left margin below line 13: 'wa-min' (opening of the next item overleaf, f. 26r)

technique_remarks: none beyond 'solved because of its ease'
plaintext_for: lines 1-3 verse follows the 25r block (8 lines on f. 25r) without a further formula; lines 12-13 verse answers the block of 7 lines on this page
certainty: medium-high for layout and verse text; medium for the first verse; sign counts approximate. Page has 13 text lines plus catchword

contents.word_groups: about 3-4 per line, roughly 20 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; introduced by 'wa-min dhalika aydan' (and of that likewise) written at the right of line 1, signs follow on the same line; alphabet of short angular signs (check marks, V, bar-and-hook, ring, a few numeral-like 5 and 3 shapes)

contents.text: فحللت ذلك سريعا وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltu dhalika sari'an wa-huwa' = I solved that quickly, and it is

contents.text: لعبدك وعد قد تقدم ذكره فله اجر وآخر شكر / وقد جمعت فيك المكارم كلها فما لك عن تاخير مكرمة عذر
contents.note: verse: 'li-'abdika wa'dun qad taqaddama dhikruhu fa-lahu ajrun wa-akharu shukr / wa-qad jumi'at fika l-makarimu kulluha fa-ma laka 'an ta'khiri makruma 'udhr' = your servant has a promise whose mention came earlier, so there is reward in it and (another) thanks; all noble qualities are gathered in you, so you have no excuse for delaying a favour. Theme (the promise 'wa'd') links it to 'an'im bi-wa'dika' on f. 25r

contents.text: ومن ذلك
contents.note: 'wa-min dhalika' = and of that: heading of the next cipher

contents.word_groups: about 5-6 per line, roughly 11 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; a different alphabet: many numeral-like signs (shapes resembling Arabic-Indic 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, a 'hah'-like ring, a comb sign); block continues overleaf (f. 26v) - only 2 lines on this page

technique_remarks: none: the formulas give only speed ('solved quickly'); no description of the trick
plaintext_for: lines 8-9 verse answers the 6-line block on this page (lines 1-6); the 2-line block at the foot (lines 11-12) has its plaintext, if any, on f. 26v
certainty: medium-high for layout and verse text; sign counts approximate. Page has 12 lines, no damage except a faint show-through

contents.word_groups: about 5 per line, roughly 20 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; continues the 2-line numeral-sign block at the foot of f. 26r (lines 11-12), so that block is 7 lines in all; alphabet of numeral-like signs (shapes like Arabic-Indic 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, H-bar, hah-ring, comb); last line only 7 signs

contents.text: فحللته سريعا وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an wa-huwa' = I solved it quickly, and it is

contents.text: ما دون بابك لي باب [?] ولا سواك لنا مثوى ولا طلب / يا خير من سمعت اذن به ورات عين ومن وفد [?] وابه
contents.note: verse, hemistich ends in -lab: 'ma duna babika li babun [al-wadhba?] wa-la siwaka lana mathwan wa-la talab' = (I have) no door but yours ..., and none but you is our lodging, nor (is there) any request; 'talab' is written on a short line of its own beneath line 7 (overflow of the first line); second line: 'ya khayra man sami'at udhnun bihi wa-ra'at 'aynun wa-man wafada [?]' = O best of those heard of by an ear and seen by an eye, and of whoever came as a delegate...; the words 'al-wadhba' (line 7) and the end of line 8 ('wafada ... wa-abihi'?) are doubtful

contents.text: ومن ذلك ايضا
contents.note: 'wa-min dhalika aydan' = and of that likewise; the small word above the left end (at line 9) reads like 'al-ward' or 'al-wird' [?], in black ink, perhaps a label for the key/alphabet - not read

contents.direction_remark: none stated; new alphabet of comb/bracket and ring-with-bars signs (several signs shaped like a table or 'm' with ring); block continues overleaf (f. 27r) or ends here - no plaintext on this page

contents.text: [cipher sign]
contents.note: a single cipher-type sign (bracket with ball head) at the very bottom left, below the last line: a catchword sign, the first sign of the next page's cipher or text

plaintext_for: lines 7-8 verse answers the numeral-sign block that began on f. 26r lines 11-12 and runs through lines 1-5 here (7 lines in all); the 3-line block at lines 10-12 has no plaintext on this page
certainty: medium: layout high; verse words partly doubtful (marked [?]); sign counts approximate; page has 12 lines

contents.word_groups: about 3 per line, roughly 14 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; no heading on this page, so this is most probably the continuation of the 3-line block at the foot of f. 26v (lines 10-12), making a block of 8 lines (not certain); alphabet of T-, Delta-, ring- and bar-shaped signs with a hook-over-line shape; first line begins with an arrow-like sign

contents.text: فحللته سريعا لسهولته وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an li-suhulatihi wa-huwa' = I solved it quickly because of its ease, and it is

contents.text: ولقد نذرت لئن رايتك سالما لاصوم لله الكريم / حذرا عليك من الزمان وصرفه حتى تعود [مسرورا؟] منصورا
contents.note: verse: 'wa-la-qad nadhartu la-in ra'aytuka saliman la-asumu li-llahi l-karim / hadharan 'alayka mina l-zamani wa-sarfihi hatta ta'uda [?]an mansura' = I vowed that if I saw you safe I would fast for God the Generous, fearing for you the Time and its turns, until you return (?) and victorious; a small interlinear word above 'ta'ud' reads 'surura' or 'suhura' [?] in black ink, an interlinear variant/correction - not certain

contents.text: ومما كتبه لي نور الدين علي بن حسين البغدادي امتحانا
contents.note: 'wa-mimma katabahu li Nur al-Din 'Ali b. Husayn al-Baghdadi imtihanan' = and of what Nur al-Din 'Ali son of Husayn al-Baghdadi wrote to me as a test

contents.direction_remark: none stated; the block is by Nur al-Din 'Ali al-Baghdadi (set as a test); alphabet of arch/hook shapes, rounded 'n'/'u' forms and a few Delta-like signs, very different from the block above

contents.text: فبقيت ايامًا لم احله لصعوبته وقلته حتى ظننت انه لا يحل ثم فتح الله خلله ففرحت به ما لم افرح بعين وهو
contents.note: 'fa-baqitu ayyaman lam ahilluhu li-su'ubatihi wa-qillatihi [?] hatta zanantu annahu la yuhallu thumma fataha llahu khallahu [?] fa-farihtu bihi ma lam afrah bi-'ayn wa-huwa' = I stayed days without solving it because of its difficulty and (its scantiness?), until I thought it could not be solved; then God opened its flaw (?) and I rejoiced in it as I never rejoiced in a 'ayn [?]; 'wa-huwa' ends the page - the solution follows on f. 27v. The words 'qillatihi', 'khallahu' and 'bi-'ayn' are doubtful

correspondents.arabic: نور الدين علي بن حسين البغدادي
correspondents.translit: Nur al-Din 'Ali b. Husayn al-Baghdadi (sent a cipher 'imtihanan', as a test)

technique_remarks: line 12-13: the compiler says he stayed days without solving Nur al-Din's block 'because of its difficulty' and nearly thought it unsolvable, then 'God opened its (flaw/gap)'; no technique named on this page
plaintext_for: lines 7-8 verse answers the 5-line block on this page (and perhaps the 3-line block at the foot of f. 26v); the answer to the Baghdadi block (lines 10-11) follows overleaf on f. 27v after 'wa-huwa'
certainty: medium: layout and names fairly clear, verse words medium, sign counts approximate. Page has 13 text lines

contents.text: شيخ البحر كلني وعلقني بسني [?]
contents.note: first line of the page after 'wa-huwa' at the foot of f. 27r: it is the (first) line of the answer to Nur al-Din al-Baghdadi's 2-line block on f. 27r; 'shaykh al-bahr kallani wa-'allaqani bi-sinni [?]' - sense and last word not secure; a very short answer (one line only), the rest of the verse is not on this page

contents.text: وكان كتب لي قبل ذلك مترجمين احدهما
contents.note: 'wa-kana kataba li qabla dhalika mutarjamayn ahaduhuma' = and he had written to me before that two translated (ciphered) pieces, one of them ... (the writer is Nur al-Din al-Baghdadi of f. 27r, presumably; the sentence is cut by the cipher and is taken up by the catchword 'wa-l-thani')

contents.word_groups: about 3-4 per line, roughly 28 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; the first of the two 'mutarjamayn'; alphabet of cross, hash (#), arrow-with-hook and '4'-like signs; lines start at right with a bare sign and end at left with a dotted divider

contents.text: فحللته سريعا وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an wa-huwa' = I solved it quickly, and it is

contents.text: يا نفس ذا الكبرياء من اين اتت [?] من مخرج السبيلين / ابوك بالامس كان من حماء وجيفة انت [?] لعدو مبين
contents.note: moral verse (humility): 'ya nafs dha l-kibriya' min ayna [?] min makhraj al-sabilayn / abuki bi-l-amsi kana min hama'in wa-jifa [?]...' = O soul, this pride, from where (does it come)? (you come) from the outlet of the two passages; your father yesterday was of mud (hama') and carrion (jifa)...; words in line 13 after 'jifa' (anta ... li-'aduwwin mubin?) are doubtful; several readings marked [?]

contents.text: والثاني
contents.note: catchword at lower left margin: 'wa-l-thani' = and the second (the second of the 'mutarjamayn'), to be the opening of f. 28r

correspondents.arabic: (implied) نور الدين علي بن حسين البغدادي
correspondents.translit: Nur al-Din 'Ali b. Husayn al-Baghdadi, continuing from f. 27r (not named again on this page)

plaintext_for: line 1: end of the answer to the Baghdadi 2-line block of f. 27r; lines 12-13: verse answers the 8-line block on this page (lines 3-10)
certainty: medium: layout high; line 1 and the verse at lines 12-13 only medium (several doubtful words); sign counts approximate. Page has 13 text lines plus catchword

contents.text: والثاني منهما
contents.note: 'wa-l-thani minhuma' = and the second of the two (the second of the two 'mutarjamayn' announced on f. 27v line 2; the catchword 'wa-l-thani' of 27v)

contents.word_groups: about 3-5 per line, roughly 28 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; the second mutarjam of the writer of f. 27v; alphabet of triple-bar (E-like) signs, triangles, small arch/'ka' shapes with a loop, a heart-shaped sign (3 times) and numeral-like 2s; last line only 4 signs (ends with a heart sign)

contents.text: فحللته سريعا لسهولته وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an li-suhulatihi wa-huwa' = I solved it quickly because of its ease, and it is

contents.text: دع الاعتراض فما الامر لك وليس لحكمك جرى الفلك / ولا تشرك بالله في حكمه فمن خاض لجة بحر هلك
contents.note: pious verse: 'da'i l-i'tirad fa-ma l-amru laka wa-laysa li-hukmika jara l-falak / wa-la tushrik bi-llahi fi hukmihi fa-man khada lujjata bahrin halak' = leave off objecting, for the matter is not yours and the heavens do not run by your judgement; and do not associate anything with God in His judgement, for whoever plunges into the deep of a sea perishes; 'bahr' in the last line slightly doubtful

contents.text: وكتب لي رفيقه
contents.note: 'wa-kataba li rafiquhu' = and his companion wrote to me (the name follows on the next page, f. 28v; 'his' presumably refers to the Baghdadi of ff. 27r-28r - not certain)

correspondents.translit: 'his companion' - a man wrote to me, name on f. 28v; identity uncertain

plaintext_for: lines 11-12 verse answers the 8-line block on this page (the second mutarjam of the Baghdadi)
certainty: medium-high for layout and verse; sign counts approximate. Page has 13 lines

contents.word_groups: about 4-5 per line, roughly 27 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; no heading on this page: the block follows 'wa-kataba li rafiquhu' at the foot of f. 28r (so it is the cipher of 'his companion'; no name is given for him on either page); alphabet of vertical single strokes ('1' shapes, very frequent), hearts (3), X, ring-with-dot, small bracket signs

contents.text: فحللته سريعا وهو من فصيحة للوزير علاء الدين عطا ملك بن الجويني اولها
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an wa-huwa min fasiha li-l-wazir 'Ala' al-Din 'Ata Malik b. al-Juwayni awwaluha' = I solved it quickly, and it is from a (fluent/eloquent) poem of the vizier 'Ala' al-Din 'Ata-Malik son of al-Juwayni (the Ilkhanid vizier and historian), its beginning (the first verses of the poem); 'fasiha' read with moderate certainty

contents.text: اذا نظر الزمان الي شزرا فلا تك ضيقا من ذاك صدرا / وكن بالله ذا ثقة لاني ارى الله في ذا الامر سرا / زماني اذ رماني لا ابالي فقد مارسته عسرا ويسرا / وقد صاحبته ستين عاما مضين وذقته حلوا ومرا
contents.note: four verse-lines, all ending in -ran (sadran, sirran, yusran, murran): 'idha nazara l-zamanu ilayya shazran fa-la taku dayyiqan min dhaka sadra / wa-kun bi-llahi dha thiqatin li-anni ara llaha fi dha l-amri sirra / zamani idh rama-ni la ubali fa-qad marastuhu 'usran wa-yusra / wa-qad sahabtuhu sittina 'aman madayna wa-dhuqtuhu hulwan wa-murra' = when Time glances at me askance, do not be narrow of heart over it; trust in God, for in this matter I see God as a secret; (my) time, when it strikes me I do not care, for I have practised it in hardship and ease; I have been with it sixty years and tasted it sweet and bitter. Some words (line 10 'ara llaha ... sirra', line 12 'madayna') medium-low certainty

contents.text: والبيتان المترجمان مما
contents.note: 'wa-l-baytan al-mutarjaman mimma' = and the two ciphered verses are of what ... (sentence runs on to f. 29r: probably 'of what [so-and-so] wrote to me')

contents.text: اذا [?]
contents.note: small catchword at lower left margin, read tentatively 'idha' or 'ada'; not clear

correspondents.arabic: الوزير علاء الدين عطا ملك بن الجويني
correspondents.translit: the vizier 'Ala' al-Din 'Ata-Malik b. al-Juwayni - NOT a correspondent: the author of the poem that the plaintext quotes (the plaintext of the companion's cipher is a verse by Juwayni)

technique_remarks: the plaintext of the block is stated to be the beginning of a poem by 'Ata-Malik al-Juwayni (the cipher was therefore a quotation, not an original composition by the sender); no trick described
plaintext_for: lines 9-12 verse answers the 6-line block on this page (lines 1-6); line 13 begins a new announcement about 'the two ciphered verses' (cipher on the following page, f. 29r)
certainty: medium: layout high, line 7-8 attribution clear enough, verse words medium (a few [?]), sign counts approximate. Page has 13 text lines plus catchword; a brown stain at line 8 left

contents.text: اذا دكت جبال الصبر دكا ترى مني فؤادا مستقرا / سواء عندي يومك دهري [?] فكن خلا وانما شئت خمرا
contents.note: two verses (rhyme -ra), directly continuing the sentence 'wa-l-baytan al-mutarjaman mimma' (the two ciphered verses ...) at the foot of f. 28v: 'idha dukkat jibalu l-sabri dakkan tara minni fu'adan mustaqirra / sawa'un 'indi yawmuka dahri [?] fa-kun khallan wa-imma shi'ta khamra' = when the mountains of patience are crushed to dust you will see in me a steady heart; all one to me, your day or my time: be vinegar, or wine if you wish. Whether these two verses are the plaintext of a cipher on f. 28v/29r is not stated; the first line may have 'dukkat' written with a doubtful first word; the second line is only medium certainty

contents.text: وكتب لي
contents.note: 'wa-kataba li' = and (someone) wrote to me; no name follows, the cipher begins on the next line

contents.word_groups: about 4-5 per line, roughly 22 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; alphabet of small connected hook/curl signs (like a ligature 'sm', 'lam-ba' shapes), 'B', 'T' and a few numeral-like 4/9/2; this is the block the compiler later says may be written 'in the language of the Egyptians'

contents.text: فحللته سريعا والبيتان للشيخ عبد العزيز الدبرني وهما
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an wa-l-baytan li-l-shaykh 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Dabrani [?] wa-huma' = I solved it quickly, and the two verses are by the shaykh 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Dabrani [?] (nisba doubtful: 'al-Dabrani/al-Dubrani'), and they are:

contents.text: ما تم الا ما يريد فدع همومك واطرح / واترك خواطرك لعل فؤادك ينشرح [?]
contents.note: two hemistichs/verses: 'ma tamma illa ma yurid fa-da' humumaka wa-trah / wa-truk khawatiraka la'alla fu'adaka yanshrah' = nothing is accomplished but what He wills, so leave your cares and cast (them) off, and leave your worries, perhaps your heart will open (be relieved); last word and 'la'alla' doubtful; a supposed rhyme in -h/-ah

contents.text: واظنها بالثاء المثلثة كتبها على لغة المصريين ولها معنى
contents.note: 'wa-azunnuha bi-l-tha' al-muthallatha katabaha 'ala lughat al-Misriyyin wa-laha ma'na' = and I think that (the cipher) was written with the three-dotted th (or: it is from the 'three-dotted' thing), in the language/dialect of the Egyptians, and it has a meaning; it follows the plaintext, so it is a remark on the 2-verse text or on the cipher just solved; sense of 'bi-l-tha' al-muthallatha' not clear to me

correspondents.translit: shaykh 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Dabrani (or al-Dubrani) [?] - named as the AUTHOR of the two verses of the plaintext, not as a sender; nisba doubtful

technique_remarks: line 13: 'written with the three-dotted tha' in the language of the Egyptians' (possibly the writing of Arabic in Egyptian pronunciation, th for another letter?) - the exact meaning is not clear; the plaintext verses are said to be by a shaykh, i.e. a quotation
plaintext_for: lines 9-12 plaintext answers the 5-line block on this page (lines 4-8); lines 1-2 are a separate verse pair continuing the 'two ciphered verses' sentence of f. 28v line 13
certainty: medium: layout high; verse words and the nisba medium-low; sign counts approximate. Page has 13 lines

contents.text: بالمثناة ايضا وكتب لي الشيخ شهاب الدين المترجم
contents.note: 'bi-l-muthannah aydan' = with the two-dotted (letter) also (continues the remark at the foot of f. 29r 'bi-l-tha' al-muthallatha ... language of the Egyptians'); 'wa-kataba li l-shaykh Shihab al-Din al-mutarjim [?]' = and the shaykh Shihab al-Din, the translator [?], wrote to me - the last word (al-mutarjim, 'the interpreter/translator', or part of the name) is read tentatively

contents.word_groups: about 4-5 per line, roughly 28 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; alphabet of numeral-like signs (8, 4, 3, 6, 9), an H-shaped sign, small 'ta-wa'-like curls and bracket signs; last line only 6 signs

contents.text: فحللتها بحضوره سريعا وكتب نسختها المقر الشريف العلائي بسط الله ظلاله فحلها سريعا واحضرها بخطه الشريف وهي
contents.note: 'fa-halaltuha bi-hudurihi sari'an wa-kataba naskhataha al-maqarr al-sharif al-'Ala'i basata llahu zilalahu fa-hallaha sari'an wa-ahdaraha bi-khattihi l-sharif wa-hiya' = I solved it quickly in his presence; and (a copy of it was written by) the noble excellency al-'Ala'i, may God extend his shade, who solved it quickly and brought it (the solution) in his noble hand, and it is: - 'al-maqarr al-sharif al-'Ala'i' is an honorific person (name not given beyond the nisba); the clause 'wa-kataba naskhataha' is read with moderate certainty

contents.text: ارى سرج الجزيرة من بعيد كلحاظ تغازل من تغازل / كان كواكب الجوزاء حطت وافرغت المنازل في المنازل [?]
contents.note: two verses: 'ara surja l-jazirati min ba'idin ka-lihazin tughazilu man tughazil / ka-anna kawakiba l-jawza'i hattat wa-afragat al-manazila fi l-manazil [?]' = I see the lamps of the island from afar like glances flirting with whom they flirt; as if the stars of Gemini had descended and emptied the mansions into the mansions; doubtful words in both lines (rhyme -il); the 'island' (al-Jazira) may be a place name (Cairo's Rawda island?) - not stated

a short catchword at the lower left margin, partly cut by the edge, not read (looks like an alif + two letters); also faint marks in the top right corner of the page (a later foliation or pen trial?), not read

correspondents.translit: shaykh Shihab al-Din al-Mutarjim (al-Mutarjam?) - the last word tentative; sender of the block
al-maqarr al-sharif al-'Ala'i - an honorific title with the nisba al-'Ala'i, he solved the cipher and brought the solution in writing (a copy-giver, not a sender)

technique_remarks: line 1 'bi-l-muthannah aydan' (with the two-dotted [letter] also) continuing 'bi-l-tha' al-muthallatha ... 'ala lughat al-Misriyyin' of f. 29r line 13: seems to say the signs/letters or the text were of dotted letters, written in Egyptian dialect; exact sense not clear; the compiler solved it 'in his (al-'Ala'i's) presence' - the block was solved in front of a high person
plaintext_for: lines 12-13 verses answer the 7-line block on this page (lines 2-8)
certainty: medium: layout high; Arabic at lines 1, 9-11 medium-high; verses 12-13 medium-low; sign counts approximate; page has 13 lines

contents.text: وكتب الشيخ شهاب الدين المترجم ايضا سجعتين / احدهما لي والاخرى للمقر الشريف العالي العلائي / بسط الله ظلاله
contents.note: 'wa-kataba l-shaykh Shihab al-Din al-mutarjim aydan saj'atayn ahaduhuma li wa-l-ukhra li-l-maqarr al-sharif al-'ali al-'Ala'i basata llahu zilalahu' = and the shaykh Shihab al-Din al-Mutarjim also wrote two rhymed-prose pieces (saj'), one of them for me and the other for the noble, lofty excellency al-'Ala'i, may God extend his shade; 'saj'atayn' and 'ahaduhuma li' read with moderate certainty (the first is 'sj'tyn' with an unusual form)

contents.word_groups: about 5-6 per line, roughly 44 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; the first of the two saj' pieces of Shihab al-Din (the one for the compiler, presumably, by the order in line 2); alphabet dominated by a very frequent U/lam-like sign with a tick (about one sign in four), plus a hook-over-bar sign, S-shapes, a '3' and numeral-like 8/4/6/9

contents.text: فحللت ذلك بحضوره سريعا لسهولته وهو
contents.note: 'fa-halaltu dhalika bi-hudurihi sari'an li-suhulatihi wa-huwa' = I solved that in his presence quickly because of its ease, and it is ('his presence' = of al-'Ala'i of line 2, apparently)

contents.text: وجارية حسناء هام [?] غلاما بفترة مقلة ونشاط قد
contents.note: start of the solution text (rhymed prose or verse): 'wa-jariyatin hasna'a ... ghulaman bi-futrati muqlatin wa-nashati qadd' = and a fair girl ... a youth with the languor of an eye and the sprightliness of a stature; the text runs on to the next page (f. 30v); the word after 'hasna'' is doubtful
a few faint marks in the top left corner above line 1 (like a later foliation or a pen trial), not read

correspondents.translit: shaykh Shihab al-Din al-Mutarjim (the same as on f. 29v; two saj' pieces)
al-maqarr al-sharif al-'ali al-'Ala'i (addressee of the second piece, may be the same person as on f. 29v)

technique_remarks: none on the trick; the text is described as 'saj'' (rhymed prose), two pieces, one for the compiler and one for al-'Ala'i; solved 'in his presence'
plaintext_for: line 13 begins the plaintext of the 8-line block on this page (lines 4-11) and runs onto f. 30v
certainty: medium: layout high; Arabic at lines 1-3 medium, line 13 medium-low; sign counts approximate. Page has 13 text lines

contents.text: رآها الشيخ فانبعث قواه وعاد الى الشباب المستجد / واتبع رده فيها نظرا فقالت ان الشيخ من اكناف نجد
contents.note: continuation of the saj' text begun on f. 30r line 13 (the girl 'ghulaman' passage): 'ra'ahaʼl-shaykh fa-inba'atha quwahu wa-'ada ila l-shabab al-mustajidd / wa-atba'a raddahu fiha nazaran fa-qalat inna l-shaykh min aknaf Najd' = the shaykh saw her and his powers revived and he returned to renewed youth; and he followed his reply on it with a look, and she said: the shaykh is from the outskirts of Najd; a playful rhymed prose in -d; reading medium-high

contents.text: واما المخدومي العلائي اسبغ الله ظلاله فانه لم يكتب / الابيات وانما كتب لنا المترجم بخطه السعيد / مولانا الشيخ من وسط نجد لا من الاكناف / فعلم الله فحلها ثم كتب له بعد ذلك
contents.note: 'wa-amma l-makhdumi l-'Ala'i asbagha llahu zilalahu fa-innahu lam yaktub al-abyat wa-innama kataba lana l-mutarjim bi-khattihi l-sa'id mawlana l-shaykh min wasat Najd la min al-aknaf fa-'alima [?] llahu fa-hallaha thumma kataba lahu ba'da dhalika' = as for my lord al-'Ala'i, may God extend his shade, he did not write the verses; rather the translator (Shihab al-Din al-Mutarjim) wrote for us in his fortunate hand 'our master the shaykh is from the middle of Najd, not from the outskirts' (a sentence read as a quotation, probably the reply/plaintext), so God knew [?] and he (the compiler or al-'Ala'i) solved it; then he wrote to him after that - the reference of the pronouns is not certain; the first part says al-'Ala'i is credited with the verses ('the verses') only by the copy but the translator is the writer of the cipher

contents.word_groups: about 4-5 per line, roughly 30 (not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; introduced by 'thumma kataba lahu ba'da dhalika' (then he wrote to him after that); alphabet of small hook/curl signs ('ha'-like curls with a tick, V and W shapes, fish-hook), with a double slash mark '//' occurring inside lines 8-10 and at line starts (probably a space/stop sign, as on f. 25r); the block has no formula or plaintext on this page, so it continues onto f. 31r or is answered there

contents.text: [cipher sign]
contents.note: a single cipher-type sign (hook-over-curve) at the lower left margin: a catchword sign for the first sign of the next page

correspondents.translit: al-mutarjim (Shihab al-Din) and my lord al-'Ala'i, again named; they are the two parties of the exchange: the first wrote the cipher by hand, the second is the 'maqarr' who solved/received it

technique_remarks: lines 3-5: the compiler states that al-'Ala'i did NOT write the verses; the translator wrote them out in his own hand (the cipher text): a note on authorship/hand of the cipher, not on the trick
plaintext_for: lines 1-2 are the end of the plaintext of the 30r block (lines 4-11 there); lines 3-6 speak of the 'verses'; the 7-line block at lines 7-13 has no plaintext on this page
certainty: medium: layout high; Arabic of lines 1-4 medium-high, lines 5-6 medium-low (pronoun reference and 'fa-'alima llahu' doubtful); sign counts approximate. Page has 13 text lines plus a catchword sign
